subject: OrchardPay — inference economics & pilot proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@orchardpay.com>, Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@orchardpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: OrchardPay — quick post-call recap and next asks

Thanks for the time today — appreciated the candid walk-through of where OrchardPay is on model costs and latency. Short recap from our side and a proposed next-step bundle so we can align on a clean pilot that tests both economics and SLA fit.

Key pain points we heard:
- High token spend on transaction classification (approx. 3.8M tokens/day last month).
- Tight p50 latency target: 250ms for single-turn classification + scoring.
- Budget tolerance for a POC: ~$12k–15k/month (finance preferred upper bound $12k).
- Ops sensitivity to implementation complexity — need a low-touch pilot that’s run by your team with Redwood ops support.

Goals you emphasized:
- Prove unit economics (tokens/$) across peak traffic and under realistic prompt lengths.
- Validate reliability: <1% error-rate regressions vs baseline and consistent latency under burst.
- Surface concrete levers (batching, prefix cache, quantization) with modeled ROI.

Initial cost levers we recommend to test in pilot:
- Continuous batching for classification to smooth latency and cut per-token execution overhead (expected 18–28% token-cost reduction for your workload mix).
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes (chat-like flows) — conservative hit-rate assumption 10–20% yields 8–12% token reduction.
- Model selection + 4-bit quantization candidate to drop raw inference $/token by ~20% when quality is acceptable.

Proposed pilot (what we can run quickly):
- 30-day pilot: Redwood-managed inference for a single production route (classification + score).
- Scope: up to 6M tokens/day peak, typical 3–4M tokens/day baseline.
- Deliverables: cost model workbook, config recommendations (batch size + cache TTL), monitoring dashboard, quality checks on your test prompts.
- Success criteria: >=25% TCO reduction vs current baseline or meet <=$12k/month at parity quality and latency.

Next asks from you:
1) Confirm budget target (you mentioned finance prefers $12k/month).
2) Share a 7‑day usage CSV for the route (I attached a sample snapshot request).
3) Approval to run the pilot under a short SOW (we’ll share draft).

Attachments: orchardpay-usage-snapshot.csv (request template) — I included a small sample to show formatting we need.

Available to sync tomorrow 11am PT if that works — otherwise we’ll aim for Wed.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.com]

From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@orchardpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@orchardpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchardPay — quick post-call recap and next asks

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Budget: finance pushed back and set a hard cap for a pilot at $12k/month unless we show guaranteed unit-cost improvements.
- Token mix: about 60% of tokens are short classification prompts (avg 24 tokens), 40% are scoring/embedding-ish flows (avg 88 tokens).
- Peak behavior: spikes during batch settlement windows — roughly 2x baseline for 10–15 minutes.

A few asks before we commit: can you model expected spend under three scenarios (no changes / batching only / batching + 15% cache hit)? We need that to justify to procurement.

If you can get a compact cost model and a proposed SOW by Wednesday EOD our procurement lead will review, and we can decide on a kickoff window (ideally late next week).

Also — happy to do the 11am PT slot tomorrow to walk the procurement person through the assumptions.

Best,
Alex
Product Ops Lead | OrchardPay
alex.zhou@orchardpay.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@orchardpay.com>, Sophie Lin <sophie.lin@orchardpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrchardPay — quick post-call recap and next asks

Alex / Sophie — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Attaching the compact cost model and a draft SOW for review (links below). Quick summary of the three scenarios (numbers are illustrative based on your token mix and measured latency distribution):

- Baseline (no changes): $18,400/mo estimated at current traffic.
- Batching only: $14,200/mo (estimated 22% reduction in per-token execution overhead).
- Batching + 15% cache hit: $11,600/mo (combined ~37% TCO reduction).

Assumptions called out in the workbook: average prompt lengths by flow, 99th-percentile end-to-end latency target (we simulate 250ms p50, some tail risk), and conservative cache hit rates (10–15%). The workbook also includes a sensitivity table for batch sizes and sequence-length mix.

Proposal for next steps:
1) Redwood shares SOW + cost workbook (attached/Drive) — please route to procurement.
2) If procurement signs off, we run a 30-day pilot with $5k Redwood credit — focus on your classification route.
3) Kickoff sync: Thu 3pm PT or Fri 11am PT (we can do one of those).

Links / attachments:
- Cost workbook & scenarios: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOrchardPayPilot
- HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/OP-2027-058
- Attachments included: orchardpay-cost-model-v1.xlsx (XLSX, 94KB), pilot-sow-draft.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

If we get procurement agreement to the $12k target, we’ll finalize the scope and lock a kickoff date. If they insist on $8–10k, we can discuss narrower scope (reduced peak handling or staged rollout).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — I’ll be on the 11am PT slot tomorrow if you want to run procurement through the model in real time.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
